simulatedPerson.name: faces
simulatedPerson.hiddenRule: Likes close shots or shallow focus (85%); dislikes extreme wide shots (10%); otherwise 25%.

interpretation.summary: Across 83 stills from 35 films, the clearest thread is closeness; you were less drawn to visible atmosphere.

sections.title: Closeness
sections.text: The stills you liked consistently share close shots (11 of 12 liked) and shallow focus (16 of 17 liked). Close framing and shallow focus separate a face or object from its surroundings, so expression and surface carry the image and the background becomes a soft field. You can see it in 12 Angry Men: Juror 3, Amélie: Amélie in the café and In the Mood for Love: Mrs Chan sips from a green teacup in the red restaurant booth.

sections.title: Visible atmosphere
sections.text: The stills you passed over consistently share veiled air (2 of 19 liked). Smoke, mist or dust in the air catches light and softens distance, so the space between camera and subject becomes visible volume. For instance The Bridge on the River Kwai: The bridge over the river at dawn, Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb: The War Room and Howl's Moving Castle: Howl's castle stalks across the moor under storm clouds.

sections.title: How sure this is
sections.text: Clear air is an early sign that more judgments could confirm or dissolve. Some characteristics cannot yet be told apart because they occur in nearly the same stills: close shots with shallow focus, artificial light with shallow focus and gaze out of frame with shallow focus. There are too few examples to say anything about patterned shadow (2 judged) and rim light (2 judged). All of this compares your own likes with your own dislikes among 83 stills; it is not a comparison with anyone else.
